(verb
  :name "entity/alive?"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "rd"
  :signature "(entity/alive? id) -> bool"
  :summary "Test whether an entity id is live (not despawned)."
  :explanation "Every entity in the world has a numeric id. Over time, entities may be killed (via entity/despawn!) and recycled. entity/alive? returns #t if the id still refers to a live entity in the world, #f if it has been despawned or never existed. This is the gate check before querying any other entity property: attempting to read entity/x, entity/kind, etc., on a dead id will return the error symbol 'entity-not-found; entity/alive? avoids that by testing presence first."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(define my-ent 7)\n(if (entity/alive? my-ent)\n  (display \"entity 7 is alive\")\n  (display \"entity 7 is dead\"))" :note "Simple presence check before acting on an entity.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (safe-query id key)\n  (if (entity/alive? id)\n    (entity/ref id key)\n    'dead))\n(safe-query 3 'health)" :note "Wrap a query in entity/alive? to avoid entity-not-found errors.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (filter pred xs)\n  (let loop ((xs xs) (acc '()))\n    (cond ((null? xs) (reverse acc))\n          ((pred (car xs)) (loop (cdr xs) (cons (car xs) acc)))\n          (else (loop (cdr xs) acc)))))\n(define (sweep-stale-refs refs)\n  (let ((live-refs (filter (lambda (r)\n    (entity/alive? r))\n    refs)))\n    (if (< (length live-refs) (length refs))\n      (display \"pruned dead refs\"))\n    live-refs))\n(define refs (list 1 2 3 4 5))\n(sweep-stale-refs refs)" :note "Periodically filter a list of entity ids, removing dead ones; avoids dangling references.")
  )
  :caveats ("entity/alive? is cheap (O(1) hash lookup), but repeated calls on the same id in a tight loop are unnecessary; cache the result." "An id that has never existed in the world returns #f, indistinguishable from a despawned id." "If an entity is despawned mid-step (deferred despawn), entity/alive? may still return #t until world/step finishes; the kill takes effect after the step.")
  :drawbacks ("Does not tell you WHY an entity is dead (never spawned vs. killed vs. expired); only whether it is alive now." "No bulk alive-check; must loop to check multiple ids.")
  :usecases ("Guard-clause: before accessing entity properties, check entity/alive? to avoid error symbols." "Reference bookkeeping: maintain lists of entity ids and periodically filter out dead ones." "State machines: check if a parent/child entity is still alive before transitioning." "Cleanup: after mass despawn, verify which ids are still live.")
  :related ("entity/despawn!" "entity/kind" "entity/ref" "entity/pos" "world/each")
  :learn (:concept "entity liveness and safe property access" :prerequisites ("world/spawn") :progression "combine with entity/kind and entity/ref to safely query dead-or-alive entities")
  :row-2-audit (
    (:problem "A projectile pool holds 200 slot ids across many frames. Some slots have been recycled since they were captured. Before reading entity/pos on any slot the code must know the slot still points at a live entity or it will get 'entity-not-found back and either crash a downstream calculation or silently poison an aggregate."
     :program "(define slots '(3 7 9 12 22))\n(define (positions ids)\n  (map (lambda (id) (if (entity/alive? id) (entity/pos id) 'skip))\n       ids))\n(display (positions slots))"
     :explanation "The map walks the id list and asks entity/alive? before each entity/pos read. Live ids get their position, dead ids get the 'skip sentinel. The downstream aggregator can filter 'skip cheaply; the important guarantee is that entity/pos is never called on a dead id, so no 'entity-not-found symbol ever slips into a numeric sum. This turns a fragile pipeline into a defensive one at the cost of one O(1) check per read."
     :meta "entity/kind would return 'entity-not-found for the dead ids and the downstream code would then have to inspect kind first, defeating the purpose. entity/ref would return the value or 'nan without telling you whether the entity is dead or the key is missing. entity/alive? is the only verb that gives an unambiguous boolean about presence.")
    (:eng "Operator lens: this is the guard-clause pattern; the SRE trace should show zero 'entity-not-found symbols leaking into the numeric layer. If one appears, the guard was missed and the pipeline is fragile." :math "Predicate over a finite set: alive? partitions entity-ids into {live, dead}; the read is defined on the live subset only." :cs "Preflight check before an operation whose failure mode is a sentinel value; same shape as fd-open-check before read()."))
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Ask whether a handle still refers to the resource it was captured for, before you use it."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity"   :code "(entity/alive? 7)")
       (:domain "process"  :code "(define (proc-alive? pid) (memv pid '(101 102 103)))\n(proc-alive? 101)")
       (:domain "set"      :code "(define (member? x s) (cond ((null? s) #f) ((equal? x (car s)) #t) (else (member? x (cdr s)))))\n(member? 7 '(3 7 9))"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: is this entity id still live in the world. Rung 2: is this process id still in the OS process table. Rung 3: is this element in a set. All three ask the same question — 'is this token a member of the current active set' — with the same shape: token in, boolean out, no mutation, cheap."
     :meta "The transfer works because set-membership is substrate-independent. Whether the set is 'live entities', 'running processes', or 'elements of a list', the check has the same signature and the same discipline: never call a use-verb on a token without first checking membership.")
    (:eng "Same shape as an ops-level 'is this container running before I docker exec'; SRE calls this a liveness probe." :math "Characteristic function of a subset: alive? : Id → {#t, #f}." :cs "Set-membership; O(1) with a hash-set, O(n) with a list; the runtime uses a hash-map keyed by id."))
  :row-4-proof (
    (:claim "Idempotence and monotone-death: alive? does not mutate state, and once an entity is despawned alive? never returns #t again for that id (until the id is recycled by a new spawn)."
     :program "(define id (world/spawn 'test 0 0))\n(define a (entity/alive? id))\n(define b (entity/alive? id))\n(entity/despawn! id)\n(world/step)\n(define c (entity/alive? id))\n(define d (entity/alive? id))\n(display (and a b (not c) (not d)))"
     :invariant "∀ id. alive?(id) is a pure function of world state; and once despawn(id) has been observed, ∀ future queries alive?(id) = #f until spawn re-uses id."
     :meta "The CS pattern is a monotone predicate over time: state flips from #t to #f once and stays. Falsified if alive? changed value across two calls with no intervening world change — that would mean the read has side effects or hidden randomness. book-of-code ch 08 (state machines) grounds monotone transitions.")
    (:eng "The operator can cache alive? across an inner loop without fear of surprise flip; SRE consequence is fewer redundant O(1) hash lookups in hot code." :math "Pure predicate; monotonically-decreasing in the death direction between spawn events." :cs "Read-only query with monotone state transition; same shape as an is-closed? probe on a channel after close()."))
  :row-5-emergence (
    (:base "entity/alive? tests whether an id still refers to a live entity."
     :composition "(define (compact-refs refs)\n  (let loop ((xs refs) (out '()))\n    (cond ((null? xs) (reverse out))\n          ((entity/alive? (car xs)) (loop (cdr xs) (cons (car xs) out)))\n          (else (loop (cdr xs) out)))))\n(define refs '(1 2 3 4 5))\n(display (compact-refs refs))"
     :emergent "A garbage-sweep over an external reference list — the caller's list stays authoritative but stale ids fall out on the next compact. The composition creates the same recognizable pattern as a weak-reference table that periodically prunes dead entries. Neither entity/alive? alone nor a naive list-walk alone gives that; the composition does."
     :meta "This is the weak-ref / periodic-sweep family, analogous to JVM WeakHashMap eviction or a Redis TTL sweep. The composition works because alive? is cheap and monotone-death (Row 4 invariant), so a periodic sweep is both correct and low-cost. book-of-composition ch 12 covers reference-liveness sweeps as a pattern.")
    (:eng "SRE cares about the sweep cadence: too frequent burns cycles, too rare lets stale refs grow; the same tradeoff as GC frequency." :math "Filter over a list by a monotone-#f-eventually predicate; the sweep converges to the set of live refs." :cs "Weak-reference table / stale-entry eviction; same shape as periodic-cache-scrub.")))

(verb
  :name "entity/bounce!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/bounce! id b) -> void"
  :summary "Set the entity's floor restitution (bounciness on ground contact)."
  :explanation "When an entity collides with the floor (set via world/floor!), the vertical velocity is scaled by a restitution coefficient. entity/bounce! sets this coefficient b ∈ [0,1]. A value of 0 means the entity sticks to the floor (no bounce); 1 means perfect elastic rebound (velocity reverses). Values in between give a damped bounce: the entity loses energy on each impact. Restitution only applies to floor collisions, not entity-to-entity collisions (which are handled by separation)."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(define ball 10)\n(entity/bounce! ball 0.8)\n(world/floor! 0 0.5)\n(world/step)" :note "Create a bouncy ball (80% restitution) above the floor, then step; it bounces back up.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (drop-and-watch id height target-bounce)\n  (entity/set-pos! id 50 height)\n  (entity/bounce! id target-bounce)\n  (world/floor! 20 0)\n  (for-each (lambda (_) (world/step))\n    (list 1 2 3 4 5)))\n(drop-and-watch 5 100 0.6)" :note "Set up a drop scenario with controlled bounce, then step 5 times to watch the decay.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (material-properties kind)\n  (cond\n    ((equal? kind 'rubber) (list 0.9 0.1))\n    ((equal? kind 'wood) (list 0.5 0.2))\n    ((equal? kind 'clay) (list 0.1 0.8))\n    (else (list 0.3 0.4))))\n(define (spawn-with-material x y kind)\n  (let* ((id (world/spawn x y 16 16))\n         (props (material-properties kind))\n         (bounce (car props))\n         (drag (cadr props)))\n    (entity/bounce! id bounce)\n    (entity/drag! id drag)\n    id))\n(spawn-with-material 50 100 'rubber)" :note "Parameterize physics by material type; bounce and drag are set together in a property table.")
  )
  :caveats ("Restitution applies only to floor contact (world/floor!); entity-to-entity collisions use separation, not bounce." "Values outside [0,1] are allowed but undefined; clamping may or may not occur in the engine." "If there is no floor, entity/bounce! has no observable effect." "Restitution interacts with drag: a high-drag entity will lose energy faster per bounce regardless of restitution coefficient.")
  :drawbacks ("No query verb to read the current restitution; it is write-only." "Bounce is isotropic (same in all directions); no way to set anisotropic restitution (e.g., different in x and y)." "High restitution (>0.8) combined with low drag can lead to perpetual bouncing, making it hard to settle the entity at rest.")
  :usecases ("Game object physics: balls, bouncy blocks, etc." "Falling-sand games: assign low restitution to sand entities to settle quickly." "Pinball and toy physics: fine-tune bounciness for feel." "Material simulation: encode material properties (rubber vs. lead) via restitution and drag.")
  :related ("world/floor!" "entity/drag!" "entity/friction!" "entity/mass!" "world/step")
  :learn (:concept "energy loss and restitution in collision response" :prerequisites ("world/floor!" "world/step" "entity/set-pos!") :progression "combine with entity/drag! for a complete material model; explore entity/friction! for sliding")
  :row-2-audit (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:problem "A falling-block puzzle drops blocks onto the floor. Blocks are supposed to STOP on impact, not chatter. If restitution is nonzero the blocks bounce forever and pile up mid-air; if we clamp velocity every frame with entity/set-vel! we override player input the same frame. The floor contact must be inelastic without touching input handling."
     :program "(define block (world/spawn 'block 100 50))\n(entity/bounce! block 0)\n(world/floor! 200 0)\n(world/step)"
     :explanation "entity/bounce! sets restitution to 0 which makes the FLOOR-contact perfectly inelastic — vertical velocity is zeroed on impact. Player input still flows through entity/accel! unchanged; only the vertical bounce channel is muted. The block falls, hits the floor, sticks; no perpetual bounce, no input suppression."
     :meta "entity/drag! damps in the air but does NOT special-case ground contact; blocks would still hit and chatter. entity/friction! damps horizontal sliding, not vertical impact. entity/set-vel! would zero every frame — including input frames. entity/bounce! is the one lever that operates ONLY at the floor-contact edge and ONLY on the vertical channel.")
    (:eng "Operator sees blocks that come to rest on first floor contact; SRE audit is: floor-contact events should produce ≤1 subsequent floor-contact per block per drop." :math "Restitution coefficient r ∈ [0,1]; vertical velocity after contact is v_after = -r · v_before; r=0 means v_after=0." :cs "Per-collision-edge multiplicative modifier; same shape as event-handler-return-value with damping factor."))
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Attenuate an outgoing signal at the reflection boundary by a coefficient in [0,1]."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity"     :code "(entity/bounce! block 0.5)")
       (:domain "acoustic"   :code "(define (echo signal r) (* r signal))\n(echo 10 0.5)")
       (:domain "linear-alg" :code "(define (reflect v r) (- (* r v)))\n(reflect 5 0.8)"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: floor contact scales bounce velocity by r. Rung 2: an acoustic wall reflection attenuates the returning wave by r. Rung 3: a linear reflection map flips sign and scales by r. All three take an incoming magnitude, negate it (for reflect), and scale by a coefficient — same one-parameter energy-loss shape."
     :meta "The transfer works because energy loss at an interface is coefficient-based across substrates. A ball, a wave, and a vector all lose the same fraction across the boundary; the physical constant r is the same interface parameter.")
    (:eng "In audio-engineering this is exactly a reflection coefficient at an impedance boundary." :math "Linear scalar map with |r|≤1 preserves stability; r=1 is lossless, r=0 is fully absorbing." :cs "Multiplicative damping factor on an event edge; same as a rate-limiter's damping term."))
  :row-4-proof (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:claim "Restitution is energy-monotone: on each floor contact, kinetic energy is multiplied by r², so total kinetic energy after n contacts is (r²)^n times the initial."
     :program "(define b (world/spawn 'ball 100 50))\n(entity/bounce! b 0.5)\n(entity/mass! b 1)\n(entity/drag! b 0)\n(entity/set-vel! b 0 10)\n(world/floor! 100 0)\n(define ke0 (let ((v (cadr (entity/vel b)))) (* 0.5 v v)))\n(world/step) (world/step) (world/step) (world/step) (world/step)\n(define ke1 (let ((v (cadr (entity/vel b)))) (* 0.5 v v)))\n(display (<= ke1 ke0))"
     :invariant "∀ contact. KE_after ≤ KE_before; more precisely KE_after = r² · KE_before when 0 ≤ r ≤ 1"
     :meta "The CS pattern is monotone-decreasing invariant per contact-event; falsified if KE after a bounce exceeded KE before — that would be a numerical or configuration bug producing free energy. book-of-motion ch 09 (collisions) grounds the coefficient-of-restitution equation.")
    (:eng "Consequence: the block will always come to rest eventually with r<1; the operator can rely on eventual stability without explicit stop logic." :math "Contraction map on kinetic energy per contact; convergent geometric series." :cs "Monotone predicate across event edges; same shape as retry-with-backoff whose backoff strictly decreases retry-budget."))
  :row-5-emergence (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:base "entity/bounce! attenuates floor-contact rebound."
     :composition "(define ball (world/spawn 'ball 100 50))\n(entity/bounce! ball 0.7)\n(entity/drag! ball 0.02)\n(entity/mass! ball 1)\n(world/gravity! 0 0.5)\n(world/floor! 300 0)\n(define (drop) (world/step))\n(on-frame drop)"
     :emergent "A pinball / bouncy-ball rest sequence — the ball bounces with progressively smaller peaks and settles into rest. Neither bounce alone nor gravity alone produces the recognizable decaying-oscillation shape; the composition does. This is the signature of a damped harmonic system, a phenomenon named 'bouncing to rest' in classical mechanics."
     :meta "This is the damped-oscillator family, analogous to a car suspension's damped rebound or an audio compressor's release envelope. book-of-motion ch 10 (energy-and-damping) covers the exact composition — restitution + gravity + drag = decaying bounce sequence.")
    (:eng "The SRE tuning knob is r versus drag: too little damping and the ball bounces for many seconds; the composition is stable but the audit tolerates only bounded time-to-rest." :math "Damped-harmonic decay envelope; peak heights follow (r²)^n." :cs "Decaying event stream with monotone amplitude; same shape as exponential-backoff-to-zero.")))

(verb
  :name "entity/collisions"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "rd"
  :signature "(entity/collisions id) -> list"
  :summary "Return a list of entity ids that collided with this entity in the last step."
  :explanation "After world/step, the physics engine resolves collisions between entities. For each entity, a collision list is built: the ids of all entities it touched during that step. entity/collisions returns this list (a Scheme list of numbers). If no collisions occurred, the list is empty. The collision log is cleared before each step, so entity/collisions reflects only the immediately previous step. This is the primary way to detect contact events in the physics loop."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(define ball 3)\n(define wall 4)\n(world/step)\n(let ((collided (entity/collisions ball)))\n  (if (null? collided)\n    (display \"no hit\")\n    (display \"hit something\")))" :note "Step the world, then check if entity 3 touched anything.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (on-collision id)\n  (let ((others (entity/collisions id)))\n    (for-each (lambda (oid)\n      (if (= oid 5)\n        (begin\n          (entity/damage! id 10)\n          (display \"took damage from special\"))))\n      others)))\n(world/step)\n(on-collision 1)" :note "After step, check collision list and apply damage if a specific enemy touched us.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (resolve-collisions id state-name)\n  (let ((collisions (entity/collisions id)))\n    (cond\n      ((null? collisions) state-name)\n      (else\n        (for-each (lambda (oid)\n          (let ((kind (entity/kind oid)))\n            (cond\n              ((equal? kind 'coin) (entity/despawn! oid))\n              ((equal? kind 'hazard) (entity/damage! id 1))\n              (else null))))\n          collisions)\n        'post-collision))))\n(world/step)\n(define next-state (resolve-collisions 7 'idle))" :note "In a state machine, check collisions and handle each type (coin, hazard) differently.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(display (entity/collisions 'hero))" :note "Which other entities bumped into the hero on the last step?")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(for-each\n  (lambda (other)\n    (entity/damage! 'hero 1))\n  (entity/collisions 'hero))" :note "Take 1 damage per collider that touched the hero this step.")
  )
  :caveats ("The collision list is cleared at the start of each world/step; a collision is only reported once (in the step it occurred)." "The list contains all entities touched, regardless of their properties (sensor, solid, etc.); use entity/kind or entity/ref to filter." "If an entity is despawned during world/step, it may or may not appear in the collision list of entities it touched; behavior is deferred-despawn dependent." "The list includes self-collisions (if somehow an entity touches itself); this is rare but possible with complex hierarchies.")
  :drawbacks ("No collision metadata (contact point, normal, penetration depth); only ids are reported." "Collisions are reported per-step; fast-moving entities may tunnel through thin colliders." "No way to distinguish between entity-to-entity and entity-to-floor collisions; must inspect entity/kind or use separate sensing." "No collision filtering at query time; must loop and check each id.")
  :usecases ("Trigger-based gameplay: detect when the player touches a coin or hazard." "Damage application: check collisions and apply damage to the appropriate entities." "State transitions: use collision lists to decide state changes (e.g., idle → hit)." "Audio/visual feedback: play a sound when a collision is detected.")
  :related ("world/step" "entity/overlaps?" "entity/sensor!" "entity/solid!" "entity/damage!")
  :learn (:concept "per-frame collision reporting and event handling" :prerequisites ("world/step" "world/spawn") :progression "combine with entity/damage! for hit logic, then explore entity/overlaps? for continuous overlap tests")
  :row-2-audit (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:problem "The hero has a hit-detection routine. After each world/step the code must list which entities the hero touched THIS frame, then apply damage per collider. Polling entity/overlaps? against every other entity would be O(n); we need the per-frame contact list the physics engine already computed."
     :program "(define (react-hits hero)\n  (for-each (lambda (oid)\n              (when (eq? (entity/kind oid) 'spike)\n                (entity/damage! hero 1)))\n            (entity/collisions hero)))\n(world/step)\n(react-hits 'hero)"
     :explanation "world/step populates each entity's collision buffer with the ids it touched during that step. entity/collisions reads that buffer. The handler walks the buffer once and applies damage per spike collider. No pairwise scan, no O(n²) sweep, no repeated overlaps? calls; the physics engine already did the work and this verb hands back the answer."
     :meta "entity/overlaps? tests a single pair right now, ignoring what happened during the step; it costs one geometric test per call and misses collisions that occurred but were resolved mid-step. world/collisions returns ALL pairs in the world, not just this hero's contacts, so filtering it is more work. entity/collisions is the per-entity contact projection that costs O(k) in this entity's contacts.")
    (:eng "SRE audit: the collision-response handler should run in time proportional to actual contacts, not to total entity count; entity/collisions is the read that guarantees that." :math "Projection from world-wide collision multiset onto the per-entity slice; cardinality k = degree of this entity in the contact graph this frame." :cs "Index-lookup on a pre-computed per-entity contact list; same shape as a per-node adjacency-list lookup after graph construction."))
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Retrieve the per-key subset of a batched event stream after the batch has completed."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity"  :code "(entity/collisions 'hero)")
       (:domain "mailbox" :code "(define (inbox-for user all) (filter (lambda (m) (equal? (car m) user)) all))\n(define (filter p xs) (cond ((null? xs) '()) ((p (car xs)) (cons (car xs) (filter p (cdr xs)))) (else (filter p (cdr xs)))))\n(inbox-for 'ada '((ada hi) (bob hey) (ada bye)))")
       (:domain "set"     :code "(define (project rel k) (map cdr (filter (lambda (r) (equal? (car r) k)) rel)))\n(project '((a 1) (a 2) (b 3)) 'a)"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: get the contact list keyed on one entity id. Rung 2: get the inbox slice for one user from the message stream. Rung 3: project a relation on the first column and filter by a key. All three are the same shape: a batched multi-key store, and a per-key projection query."
     :meta "The transfer works because per-key projection is substrate-independent. A collision buffer, a mailbox, and a relational table all support the same query; only the substrate differs.")
    (:eng "In operator language this is the shape of a fanned-out event bus with per-subscriber inboxes." :math "Projection on the first coordinate of a bag of ordered pairs." :cs "Group-by / index-lookup; O(1) for pre-indexed, O(n) otherwise."))
  :row-4-proof (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:claim "Symmetry of collision reporting: if id A appears in entity/collisions of id B for a given step, then B appears in entity/collisions of A for that same step."
     :program "(define a (world/spawn 'a 100 100))\n(define b (world/spawn 'b 100 100))\n(entity/solid! a #t) (entity/solid! b #t)\n(world/step)\n(define a-in-b (memv a (entity/collisions b)))\n(define b-in-a (memv b (entity/collisions a)))\n(display (equal? (if a-in-b #t #f) (if b-in-a #t #f)))"
     :invariant "∀ step s, ids a b. (a ∈ collisions(b)@s) ⇔ (b ∈ collisions(a)@s)"
     :meta "The CS pattern is a symmetric relation over ids at each step; falsified if A saw B but B did not see A — that would indicate a bookkeeping bug in the physics solver. book-of-code ch 05 (relations) grounds symmetric-relation properties.")
    (:eng "Consequence: either entity can be treated as the primary in a two-sided response (damage + knockback); operator does not have to guess which side reports the pair." :math "Symmetric binary relation on the id set per step." :cs "Undirected edge in the per-step contact graph; both endpoints hold the edge."))
  :row-5-emergence (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:base "entity/collisions returns the per-frame contact list for one entity."
     :composition "(define (damage-router hero)\n  (for-each (lambda (oid)\n              (case (entity/kind oid)\n                ((spike)  (entity/damage! hero 1))\n                ((coin)   (entity/despawn! oid))\n                ((portal) (entity/set-pos! hero 0 0))\n                (else '())))\n            (entity/collisions hero)))\n(world/step)\n(damage-router 'hero)"
     :emergent "A collision-based event dispatcher — the hero has one contact input and multiple typed reactions branching by other-kind. The pattern IS an event-router keyed on typed messages, a familiar analog to a switch-router in Redux or ON DELETE CASCADE polyalternative rules in SQL."
     :meta "This is the event-dispatch family; book-of-composition ch 10 (dispatch-and-routers) covers exactly this shape. The composition works because entity/collisions gives a clean per-frame batch and entity/kind gives a typed discriminator; together they enable a compile-time-checkable case dispatch.")
    (:eng "SRE lens: each contact fires exactly once per step; audit logs should show one damage/coin/portal event per contact edge per step, no duplicates." :math "Dispatch table indexed by discriminator; same shape as an FSM transition table." :cs "Event router; same shape as fork-choose-close in an event handler.")))

(verb
  :name "entity/damage!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/damage! id hp-loss) -> void"
  :summary "Subtract hit points from an entity; if hp ≤ 0, emit 'entity/died and despawn."
  :explanation "Entities can have hit points (set via entity/hp!). entity/damage! subtracts a value from the current hp. If the result is ≤ 0, the entity emits an 'entity/died event and is queued for despawn (deferred if mid-step). If hp stays above 0, the entity survives with reduced health. This is the primary way to model health/damage in combat or hazard systems."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(define enemy 8)\n(entity/hp! enemy 50)\n(entity/damage! enemy 20)\n(display (entity/ref enemy 'hp))" :note "Set enemy to 50 hp, damage by 20, read back 30 hp.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (check-enemy-health id)\n  (entity/damage! id 5)\n  (let ((hp (entity/ref id 'hp)))\n    (cond\n      ((null? hp) (display \"no hp tracked\"))\n      ((<= hp 0) (display \"enemy dead\"))\n      ((< hp 20) (display \"enemy critical\"))\n      (else (display \"enemy ok\")))))\n(entity/hp! 5 100)\n(check-enemy-health 5)" :note "Damage and then branch on health state.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define do-death-feedback (lambda args (list \"do-death-feedback\" args)))\n(define (on-projectile-hit target-id proj-id)\n  (let ((damage (entity/ref proj-id 'power)))\n    (entity/damage! target-id damage)\n    (entity/despawn! proj-id)\n    (if (entity/alive? target-id)\n      (do-hit-feedback target-id)\n      (do-death-feedback target-id))))\n(define proj 10)\n(entity/set! proj 'power 15)\n(define target 20)\n(entity/hp! target 100)\n(on-projectile-hit target proj)" :note "Hit detection: read damage from projectile, apply to target, despawn projectile, branch on target survival.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(entity/damage! 'enemy 5)" :note "Take 5 hp off the enemy. If that puts them at or below zero, they die.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (sword-hit target)\n  (entity/damage! target 10))\n(sword-hit 'goblin)" :note "Wrap the damage call in a named attack for readability.")
  )
  :caveats ("entity/damage! emits 'entity/died silently via the event system; there is no immediate callback. You must listen for the event or check entity/alive? after the step." "The entity is despawned deferred (at the end of the step if mid-step, immediately otherwise); it may still appear in collision lists of other entities in the same step." "If the entity has no hp set, entity/ref returns 'nan or null; entity/damage! may treat it as 0 (exact behavior is implementation-dependent)." "Negative damage (healing) is not prevented; entity/damage! with a negative value will add hp. Use a separate heal function if needed." "If called on a dead entity (entity/alive? returns #f), the call is a no-op.")
  :drawbacks ("No return value; you cannot query the new hp without a separate entity/ref call." "No damage modifiers (armor, resistance, vulnerability); all damage is applied equally." "The 'entity/died event is not queryable before the entity is fully removed; some cleanup may be deferred." "No damage cap or max hp enforcement at the entity/damage! level; hp can go arbitrarily negative if repeatedly damaged.")
  :usecases ("Combat: apply weapon/spell damage to enemies." "Hazards: reduce player hp when touching spikes, lava, etc." "Degradation: reduce health over time (poison, hunger)." "Boss phases: trigger state changes when hp crosses thresholds.")
  :related ("entity/hp!" "entity/despawn!" "entity/alive?" "entity/ref" "entity/collisions")
  :learn (:concept "deferred health depletion and death events" :prerequisites ("entity/hp!" "entity/despawn!") :progression "combine with entity/collisions for collision-based damage, then explore state machines for health-based AI")
  :row-2-audit (
    (:problem "Every projectile that lands on an enemy should subtract enemy hp and, if hp drops to zero, delete the enemy and emit 'entity/died. Doing this by hand (read hp, subtract, check ≤0, despawn, emit) is four calls and easy to skip one; the correct answer is one atomic verb."
     :program "(define e (world/spawn 'enemy 50 50))\n(entity/hp! e 20)\n(entity/damage! e 25)\n(display (entity/alive? e))"
     :explanation "entity/damage! reads hp, subtracts, compares to zero, emits 'entity/died if triggered, and queues the despawn. The whole life-cycle transition happens inside one verb call. The display then reads #f because the entity was killed."
     :meta "entity/hp! only SETS the value; it does not subtract or check. entity/despawn! kills immediately but skips the damage accounting and event. Doing it by hand splits the responsibility across three sites where a bug in one site desyncs the others. entity/damage! is the packaged transition.")
    (:eng "SRE consequence: the 'entity/died event is guaranteed to fire exactly when hp crosses zero, so downstream listeners (loot drops, score) do not miss a death or fire twice." :math "Threshold-crossing detector: emits event when hp_new ≤ 0 < hp_old." :cs "Atomic read-modify-write with side effect; same shape as compareAndSet."))
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Deduct from a bounded resource; if it crosses zero, emit an event."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity"  :code "(entity/damage! e 5)")
       (:domain "credit"  :code "(define bal 100) (define (spend n) (set! bal (- bal n)) (if (<= bal 0) 'overdraft 'ok))\n(spend 120)")
       (:domain "monoid"  :code "(define (deduct v x) (max 0 (- v x)))\n(deduct 10 15)"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: hp decrement with death-event. Rung 2: balance decrement with overdraft-event. Rung 3: bounded-subtract that saturates at zero. Same shape: bounded quantity, subtractive update, threshold event."
     :meta "Every bounded resource with a zero-cross event has this shape. The substrate changes (hp, credit, integer), the shape stays.")
    (:eng "SRE calls this a leaky-bucket zero-alarm; audit signals when the value crosses the floor." :math "Truncated subtraction over N; monoid with saturating identity." :cs "Bounded counter; same shape as a semaphore's tryAcquire that emits on exhaustion."))
  :row-4-proof (
    (:claim "Monotonicity: damage!(e, x) with x ≥ 0 never increases hp; consecutive damages sum: damage!(e, a); damage!(e, b) is equivalent (in hp reduction) to damage!(e, a+b) if the entity survives both."
     :program "(define e (world/spawn 'x 0 0))\n(entity/hp! e 100)\n(entity/damage! e 10)\n(entity/damage! e 20)\n(define h1 (entity/ref e 'hp))\n(define f (world/spawn 'x 0 0))\n(entity/hp! f 100)\n(entity/damage! f 30)\n(define h2 (entity/ref f 'hp))\n(display (equal? h1 h2))"
     :invariant "∀ e a b. survive? ⇒ hp(damage(damage(e,a),b)) = hp(damage(e, a+b))"
     :meta "The CS pattern is homomorphism from (nonneg reals, +) to (hp-decrements, ∘). Falsified if two 5-hp hits left hp higher or lower than one 10-hp hit — that would mean hidden per-call overhead in the damage transition. book-of-math ch 07 (monoids) grounds the additive structure.")
    (:eng "Consequence: rebinning damage per-frame (batch tick vs. per-hit) does not change survival outcome, so the operator can optimize batching freely." :math "Monoid morphism between (ℝ≥0, +) and hp-transitions." :cs "Composable reducer; same shape as accumulating counter decrement."))
  :row-5-emergence (
    (:base "entity/damage! subtracts hp and fires death when hp ≤ 0."
     :composition "(define proj (world/spawn 'bullet 0 0))\n(entity/set! proj 'power 15)\n(define (on-hit target proj)\n  (entity/damage! target (entity/ref proj 'power))\n  (entity/despawn! proj))\n(on-hit 'enemy proj)"
     :emergent "A hit-detection / weapon-effect chain — projectile carries power as payload, on-hit reads it and applies as damage, projectile then despawns. The pattern is the classic 'projectile carries typed payload, target applies typed effect' shape common to every weapon system in every game framework."
     :meta "This is the payload-carrying-event family, analogous to a Redux action carrying a payload interpreted by a reducer. book-of-composition ch 09 (payload-and-effect) covers exactly this shape. Works because entity/set!/entity/ref decouple payload from execution and entity/damage! is the effector.")
    (:eng "SRE audit: every despawn of a projectile should be paired with exactly one damage application; leaked projectiles or double-applications are configuration bugs." :math "Message-carrying transducer; payload dictates the coefficient of the state transition." :cs "Command with payload; same shape as an event-with-data emitted onto a bus.")))

(verb
  :name "entity/despawn!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/despawn! id) -> void"
  :summary "Kill an entity and remove it from the world (deferred if mid-step)."
  :explanation "When you want an entity to disappear, call entity/despawn!. The entity is marked for deletion; if called during world/step, the deletion is deferred until the step completes (to avoid invalidating collision lists). Otherwise, it happens immediately. After despawn, entity/alive? returns #f and the id is recycled. This is the primary way to remove entities cleanly."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(define particle 15)\n(entity/despawn! particle)\n(if (entity/alive? particle)\n  (display \"still alive\")\n  (display \"dead\"))" :note "Despawn an entity and check it is gone.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (projectile-hit-target proj target)\n  (entity/damage! target 10)\n  (entity/despawn! proj))\n(world/step)\n(projectile-hit-target 3 5)" :note "After a collision (detected in step), damage the target and remove the projectile.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (lifetime-expire id lifetime-ms elapsed-ms)\n  (if (>= elapsed-ms lifetime-ms)\n    (begin\n      (entity/despawn! id)\n      #t)\n    #f))\n(define particles (list 10 11 12))\n(for-each (lambda (p)\n  (let ((age (entity/ref p 'age)))\n    (if (null? age) (entity/set! p 'age 0))\n    (entity/set! p 'age (+ (entity/ref p 'age) 16))\n    (lifetime-expire p 1000 (entity/ref p 'age))))\n  particles)" :note "Age particles each frame; despawn when lifetime is reached.")
  )
  :caveats ("If called during world/step (e.g., in a collision handler), the despawn is deferred; the entity remains alive until the step completes." "Calling entity/despawn! on an already-dead entity is a no-op." "The entity id is recycled; if you store old ids and do not check entity/alive?, you may refer to a different entity that was spawned later with the same id." "Despawning an entity does not automatically remove references to it from other entities (e.g., parent/child links); use entity/parent! to detach children if needed.")
  :drawbacks ("No return value; you cannot check if the despawn succeeded." "Deferred despawn means the entity is still queryable (alive, position, etc.) until the step finishes; cleanup that relies on immediate removal must be done explicitly." "No way to revert a despawn once called (no 'resurrect' verb); design for one-way lifecycles." "If a child entity is despawned while attached to a parent, the parent reference becomes dangling; manual cleanup is needed.")
  :usecases ("Projectile impact: despawn the projectile when it hits something." "Lifetime expiry: despawn particles or effects after a set time." "Hazard triggers: despawn the player on contact with spikes." "Bulk cleanup: despawn all enemies at the end of a level.")
  :related ("world/spawn" "entity/alive?" "entity/damage!" "entity/parent!" "world/step")
  :learn (:concept "deferred entity removal and id recycling" :prerequisites ("world/spawn" "world/step") :progression "combine with entity/damage! for health-based removal, then explore entity/parent! for hierarchical cleanup")
  :row-2-audit (
    (:problem "A particle system spawns 200 particles per second. Each particle has a lifetime; after N frames the particle should disappear cleanly without invalidating any collision list that is being iterated right now."
     :program "(define (age-and-kill p)\n  (let ((age (or (entity/ref p 'age) 0)))\n    (entity/set! p 'age (+ age 1))\n    (when (>= age 30) (entity/despawn! p))))\n(world/each age-and-kill)\n(world/step)"
     :explanation "The lifetime check increments age each frame and calls despawn! when the ceiling is reached. Because despawn! is deferred when called during iteration, the collision buffer that world/each is walking is not mutated mid-loop; the actual removal happens at the end of the current step."
     :meta "entity/damage! ties removal to hp accounting and fires 'entity/died; particles have no combat semantics so damage! is the wrong verb. Setting a dead-flag manually leaves the entity live in queries. entity/despawn! is the honest verb for lifetime expiry.")
    (:eng "SRE audit: entity/count should decrement by the number of expired particles each step, no more no less." :math "Domain restriction: the alive-set loses one element per despawn!, no more." :cs "Deferred delete; same shape as a mark-and-sweep GC's marking phase."))
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Mark for deletion during iteration, actually delete after the iteration completes."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity"     :code "(entity/despawn! p)")
       (:domain "list"       :code "(define (mark-and-sweep xs pred)\n  (let loop ((xs xs) (keep '()))\n    (cond ((null? xs) (reverse keep))\n          ((pred (car xs)) (loop (cdr xs) keep))\n          (else (loop (cdr xs) (cons (car xs) keep))))))\n(mark-and-sweep '(1 2 3 4) even?)")
       (:domain "hashmap"    :code "(define (delete-if h pred)\n  (define keys (hash/keys h))\n  (for-each (lambda (k) (when (pred k) (hash/remove! h k))) keys)\n  h)\n(define h (hash/make)) (hash/set! h 'a 1) (hash/set! h 'b 2)\n(delete-if h (lambda (k) (eq? k 'a)))"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: mark entity for removal, engine sweeps after step. Rung 2: mark items during traversal, produce clean list at end. Rung 3: gather keys first, then delete outside the iterating loop. Same shape: don't mutate the collection you are walking."
     :meta "The transfer works because 'don't mutate during iteration' is a shape-level discipline, not a substrate-specific rule.")
    (:eng "Same shape as SRE's 'no config change during rollout'; safe removal happens at boundaries." :math "Sweep at fixed-point of iteration; deletion is a monotone shrink." :cs "Deferred delete pattern; same shape as ConcurrentModificationException-avoidance."))
  :row-4-proof (
    (:claim "Idempotence: calling despawn! twice on the same id is equivalent to calling it once; alive? returns #f after either."
     :program "(define e (world/spawn 'x 0 0))\n(entity/despawn! e)\n(entity/despawn! e)\n(world/step)\n(display (entity/alive? e))"
     :invariant "∀ id. despawn(despawn(id)) ≡ despawn(id) (with respect to alive-set membership)"
     :meta "The CS pattern is idempotence — repeating the operation is safe. Falsified if two despawn! calls left the world in a state distinguishable from one despawn! call. book-of-code ch 06 (idempotence) grounds the definition.")
    (:eng "Consequence: cleanup code can call despawn! defensively without tracking whether the entity was already killed." :math "Idempotent operation: op ∘ op = op." :cs "Idempotent write; same shape as HTTP PUT."))
  :row-5-emergence (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:base "entity/despawn! marks an entity for removal after the current step."
     :composition "(define (fire-projectile x y dx dy)\n  (let ((p (world/spawn 'proj x y)))\n    (entity/set-vel! p dx dy)\n    (world/after 60 'expire p)))\n(fire-projectile 0 0 5 0)\n(on-event 'expire (lambda (id) (entity/despawn! id)))"
     :emergent "A timed-lifetime resource — projectile spawns, world/after schedules an expiration event, the handler despawns it. The pattern is a TTL (time-to-live) resource, the same family as a Redis key with EXPIRE, or a session token with lifetime."
     :meta "This is the ephemeral-resource family; book-of-composition ch 11 (lifetime-management) covers scheduled-expiry. Works because world/after supplies the scheduler and despawn! is the executor.")
    (:eng "SRE cares that TTL fires exactly once per entity; leaked projectiles are entities whose TTL handler never ran." :math "Bounded-lifetime resource; monotone-death." :cs "TTL cache pattern; same shape as expire-and-remove.")))

(verb
  :name "entity/distance"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "rd"
  :signature "(entity/distance id1 id2) -> number"
  :summary "Return the Euclidean distance between two entities."
  :explanation "Often you need to know how far apart two entities are: for targeting, threat assessment, or proximity checks. entity/distance computes the straight-line distance between the positions of two entities. Internally, it reads both positions (via entity/pos) and returns sqrt((x1-x2)² + (y1-y2)²). If either entity is dead, the distance is undefined (typically returns a sentinel or error symbol)."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(define player 1)\n(define enemy 2)\n(let ((d (entity/distance player enemy)))\n  (if (< d 50)\n    (display \"enemy close\")\n    (display \"enemy far\")))" :note "Check if two entities are within a threat range.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (find-nearest searcher others)\n  (let ((min-dist 999999)\n        (nearest #f))\n    (for-each (lambda (oid)\n      (let ((d (entity/distance searcher oid)))\n        (if (and (number? d) (< d min-dist))\n          (begin\n            (set! min-dist d)\n            (set! nearest oid)))))\n      others)\n    nearest))\n(find-nearest 1 (list 2 3 4 5))" :note "Scan a list of entities and return the id of the closest one.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (filter pred xs)\n  (let loop ((xs xs) (acc '()))\n    (cond ((null? xs) (reverse acc))\n          ((pred (car xs)) (loop (cdr xs) (cons (car xs) acc)))\n          (else (loop (cdr xs) acc)))))\n(define (threat-level searcher targets)\n  (let ((threats (filter (lambda (t)\n    (let ((d (entity/distance searcher t)))\n      (and (number? d) (< d 100))))\n    targets)))\n    (map (lambda (t)\n      (let ((d (entity/distance searcher t))\n            (kind (entity/kind t)))\n        (list t kind d)))\n      threats)))\n(threat-level 1 (list 2 3 4 5 6))" :note "Enumerate all nearby targets (within 100 units) and return a threat list with kinds and distances.")
  )
  :caveats ("entity/distance reads positions synchronously; if you call it many times in a tight loop, consider caching results." "If either id is dead, entity/distance may return a sentinel (e.g., 'entity-not-found) or a very large number; always guard with number? or null?." "The distance is computed in 2D; there is no z (depth) component." "Distance is symmetric: entity/distance a b equals entity/distance b a.")
  :drawbacks ("Requires both entities to be alive; no fault-tolerance for dead ids." "Expensive to call on large groups (O(n) for n entities); use spatial hashing (e.g., ai/grid) for many queries." "Returns only magnitude, not the vector; for steering or directional effects, compute (dx, dy) separately or use ai/seek.")
  :usecases ("Targeting and range checks: is the player within firing range?" "Threat assessment: rank enemies by distance." "Pathfinding: compute distance to goal for heuristics." "Proximity triggers: activate an effect when two entities are close.")
  :related ("entity/pos" "entity/overlaps?" "ai/seek" "ai/arrive" "entity/collisions")
  :learn (:concept "spatial distance queries for targeting and proximity" :prerequisites ("entity/pos" "entity/alive?") :progression "use in simple guards, then combine with filtering for threat lists, then explore ai/seek for distance-based steering")
  :row-2-audit (
    (:problem "An enemy AI needs to decide 'chase' vs 'idle' based on whether the player is inside a threat range. Recomputing sqrt((dx*dx)+(dy*dy)) inline works but scatters math and misses the sentinel-when-dead case; a single verb that returns the number or a checkable value is cleaner."
     :program "(define (choose-mode enemy player)\n  (let ((d (entity/distance enemy player)))\n    (cond ((not (number? d)) 'idle)\n          ((< d 100) 'chase)\n          (else 'idle))))\n(display (choose-mode 'enemy 'player))"
     :explanation "entity/distance reads both positions and returns Euclidean magnitude, or a sentinel if either id is dead. The cond checks number? first to catch the dead case, then compares against a threat threshold. One verb call, one branch, no inline arithmetic."
     :meta "entity/pos gives coordinates but forces you to write the sqrt yourself; entity/overlaps? tests AABB intersection not radius; ai/seek would compute the direction but requires a live target. entity/distance is the read that answers 'how far'.")
    (:eng "SRE consequence: distance-based AI decisions run in O(1) per query rather than per-pair scanning; audit tolerates dead-target sentinel." :math "Euclidean metric on ℝ²." :cs "Fold of coordinate deltas into a scalar; same shape as np.linalg.norm."))
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Reduce a pair of coordinate vectors to a single scalar magnitude of their difference."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity"  :code "(entity/distance 'a 'b)")
       (:domain "geom"    :code "(define (dist p q) (sqrt (+ (expt (- (car p) (car q)) 2) (expt (- (cadr p) (cadr q)) 2))))\n(dist '(0 0) '(3 4))")
       (:domain "metric"  :code "(define (l2 xs ys) (sqrt (apply + (map (lambda (x y) (expt (- x y) 2)) xs ys))))\n(l2 '(1 2) '(4 6))"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: entity distance. Rung 2: 2D geometric distance. Rung 3: general L2 norm on n-dimensional points. Same shape: two vectors go in, scalar magnitude of difference comes out."
     :meta "The transfer works because distance is defined by the metric axioms, substrate-independent.")
    (:eng "SRE lens: any distance metric with the triangle inequality is a valid substitute for optimization purposes." :math "Metric space; ρ(a,b)=ρ(b,a), ρ(a,b)=0⇔a=b, ρ(a,c)≤ρ(a,b)+ρ(b,c)." :cs "Pairwise magnitude; same shape as ||u-v|| in a vector library."))
  :row-4-proof (
    (:claim "Symmetry and non-negativity: entity/distance(a,b) = entity/distance(b,a) ≥ 0; equals zero iff both entities are at the same position."
     :program "(define a (world/spawn 'x 10 20))\n(define b (world/spawn 'x 40 60))\n(define d1 (entity/distance a b))\n(define d2 (entity/distance b a))\n(display (and (equal? d1 d2) (>= d1 0)))"
     :invariant "∀ a b. distance(a,b) = distance(b,a) ∧ distance(a,b) ≥ 0"
     :meta "The CS pattern is a metric — obeys the identity, symmetry, and non-negativity axioms. Falsified if distance(a,b) ≠ distance(b,a). book-of-math ch 11 (metric-spaces) grounds the axioms.")
    (:eng "Consequence: the operator can pass either argument first without changing semantics; caching key can be sorted-pair to dedupe." :math "Symmetric non-negative bilinear form on coordinate differences." :cs "Symmetric pure function; same shape as string-compare(a,b) = -string-compare(b,a) for order but here for magnitude."))
  :row-5-emergence (
    (:base "entity/distance returns Euclidean distance between two entities."
     :composition "(define (nearest-of self others)\n  (let loop ((xs others) (best #f) (bd 1e18))\n    (cond ((null? xs) best)\n          ((let ((d (entity/distance self (car xs))))\n             (and (number? d) (< d bd)))\n           (loop (cdr xs) (car xs) (entity/distance self (car xs))))\n          (else (loop (cdr xs) best bd)))))\n(display (nearest-of 'hero '(a b c)))"
     :emergent "A nearest-neighbour search over a candidate set. The pattern IS argmin-by-distance, the classic shape shared with k-NN queries, spatial-index lookups, and physics broad-phase culling."
     :meta "This is the argmin-search family; book-of-composition ch 07 (search-and-select) grounds. Works because distance is a total order-like scalar and the fold is a monotone reducer.")
    (:eng "SRE lens: O(n) linear scan; for large n, spatial index turns this into O(log n) but the shape is the same." :math "Argmin over a finite set with respect to a metric." :cs "Fold-with-companion-value; same shape as reduce with min-by.")))

(verb
  :name "entity/drag!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/drag! id d) → void"
  :summary "Set air resistance on an entity; controls how quickly it loses velocity."
  :explanation "Drag simulates air friction: a high value (close to 1) makes the entity slow down gradually and feel floaty; a low value (close to 0) is nearly frictionless. The value d must be in [0, 1]. This is per-entity and independent of the world gravity or floor. Use it to tune how a body decelerates naturally after forces stop being applied."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((ball (world/spawn 'ball 100 100)))\n  (entity/drag! ball 0.1)\n  (world/step))" :note "Low drag (0.1) lets the ball glide freely; it will coast a long distance before stopping.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(let ((feather (world/spawn 'feather 50 50))\n      (stone (world/spawn 'stone 150 50)))\n  (entity/drag! feather 0.8)\n  (entity/drag! stone 0.05)\n  (entity/accel! feather 10 0)\n  (entity/accel! stone 10 0)\n  (world/step))" :note "Feather (high drag) decelerates sharply; stone (low drag) maintains momentum longer.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (spawn-with-air-feel kind weight)\n  (let ((ent (world/spawn kind 100 100)))\n    (entity/mass! ent weight)\n    (entity/drag! ent (/ weight (+ weight 1)))\n    (entity/friction! ent 0.05)\n    ent))\n(spawn-with-air-feel 'heavy-box 5)" :note "Drag is scaled with mass to create a physical feel: heavier bodies get proportionally higher drag for visual plausibility.")
  )
  :caveats ("Drag acts every frame multiplicatively; it is NOT the same as friction! (which is per-step velocity decay on ground contact)." (verb
  :name "entity/ref"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "rd"
  :signature "(entity/ref id key) → value | 'nan"
  :summary "Retrieve a per-entity scratch value by key; returns the special value 'nan if the key does not exist."
  :explanation "Each entity is a store for arbitrary per-entity user data, accessed by key (usually a symbol or string). entity/ref reads a value without modifying it. If the key does not exist, it returns the symbol 'nan (not the number NaN; this is a sentinel). Use this to attach state metadata to entities: team membership, cooldowns, behavior flags, or game-specific counters. Pair with entity/set! (or entity/set!) to write."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((npc (world/spawn 'npc 100 100)))\n  (entity/set! npc 'cooldown 10)\n  (display (entity/ref npc 'cooldown)))" :note "Set a cooldown value on the NPC and read it back; will print 10.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (decrement-cooldown id)\n  (let ((cd (entity/ref id 'cooldown)))\n    (if (equal? cd 'nan)\n      'nan\n      (entity/set! id 'cooldown (- cd 1)))))\n(let ((enemy (world/spawn 'enemy 50 50)))\n  (entity/set! enemy 'cooldown 5)\n  (decrement-cooldown enemy)\n  (display (entity/ref enemy 'cooldown)))" :note "Check if cooldown exists before decrementing; returns 4.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (handle-attack-ready entity)\n  (let ((cd (entity/ref entity 'attack-cooldown)))\n    (cond ((equal? cd 'nan)\n           (entity/set! entity 'attack-cooldown 30)\n           'attacked)\n          ((> cd 0)\n           (entity/set! entity 'attack-cooldown (- cd 1))\n           'cooling)\n          (else\n           (entity/set! entity 'attack-cooldown 30)\n           'attacked))))\n(let ((boss (world/spawn 'boss 200 200)))\n  (display (handle-attack-ready boss))\n  (display (handle-attack-ready boss)))" :note "State machine using per-entity storage: first call returns 'attacked and sets cooldown; second call returns 'cooling.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(display (entity/ref 'hero 'combo))" :note "Read a per-entity scratch value. If nothing was stored, you get 'nan.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(let ((score (entity/ref 'hero 'score)))\n  (if (eq? score 'nan)\n      (display \"no score yet\")\n      (display score)))" :note "Guard against the 'nan sentinel so a missing key doesn't crash your logic.")
  )
  :caveats ("Missing keys return 'nan (the symbol), not 'nan as a number; check with (equal? val 'nan) not (number? val)." "entity/ref returns the exact value stored; no coercion or type checking." "The scratch map is per-entity and is NOT serialized in world snapshots (transient).")
  :drawbacks ("No automatic cleanup of stale keys; orphaned data can accumulate if you do not explicitly remove old entries." "Key collisions are silent: if two systems use the same key name, they overwrite each other." "Performance is O(1) per lookup, but iterating many entities and reading the same key is slower than a separate data structure.")
  :usecases ("Storing per-entity state: cooldowns, health status, behavior flags, quest progress." "Attaching metadata without modifying the entity's position, velocity, or collision properties." "Game logic that needs to track custom properties across multiple frames.")
  :related ("entity/set!" "entity/tag!" "group/find")
  :learn (:concept "Per-entity key-value storage as a read-only query." :prerequisites ("world/spawn" "entity/kind") :progression "Use entity/ref to read; then learn entity/set! to write. Later, use entity/tag! for group-based queries.")
  :row-2-audit (
    (:problem "A boss AI's attack cooldown must be checked each tick. The value lives in per-entity scratch. Direct lookup with entity/ref returns the value or 'nan if never set — no dictionary API to memorize, no key not found exception."
     :program "(define b (world/spawn 'boss 100 100))\n(entity/set! b 'cd 30)\n(let ((cd (entity/ref b 'cd)))\n  (display (if (eq? cd 'nan) 'unset cd)))"
     :explanation "entity/ref reads the value at key 'cd. If never set, returns 'nan (a symbol sentinel), so we branch on eq?. One call, one sentinel check."
     :meta "entity/set! writes; entity/ref reads. entity/tag! is for group membership not scalar values. entity/kind gives the type symbol not scratch. For scalar per-entity state, entity/ref is the read.")

     :rungs (

       (:domain "cache"  :code "(define c '((a . 1) (b . 2))) (define (lookup k xs) (cond ((null? xs) 'miss) ((eq? (caar xs) k) (cdar xs)) (else (lookup k (cdr xs)))))\n(lookup 'a c)"))
     :explanation "Rung 1: per-entity scratch. Rung 2: hashmap lookup with default. Rung 3: associative-list lookup. Same shape: key→value with sentinel-on-miss."
     :meta "Substrate-independent: every kv store has this read.")

(verb
  :name "entity/goto!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/goto! id state) → void"
  :summary "Transition an entity to a new state; emits 'entity/state-change event."
  :explanation "entity/goto! is a finite-state-machine (FSM) primitive: it changes an entity's current state (stored internally) to a new one and emits an 'entity/state-change event. The state is typically a symbol like 'idle, 'running, 'jumping, 'dead. This is separate from game-logic state (use entity/set! for that); the FSM state is the entity's animation or behavior mode. Listeners (via card/emit, act, or similar event handlers) receive the event and can branch logic. Use entity/state to read the current state."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((player (world/spawn 'player 100 100)))\n  (entity/goto! player 'idle)\n  (entity/goto! player 'running))" :note "Transition the player from idle to running; 'entity/state-change is emitted twice.")

(verb
  :name "entity/gravity-scale!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/gravity-scale! id s) → void"
  :summary "Set the per-body gravity multiplier; 0 floats, 1 is normal, >1 is heavy."
  :explanation "entity/gravity-scale! controls how much an entity is affected by the world's gravity. A scale of 0 means the entity ignores gravity and floats freely. A scale of 1 (default) means normal gravity acceleration. A scale >1 means heavier gravity (e.g., 2.0 = double gravity). This is the primary knob for tuning embodiment and relative weight without changing the world gravity or the entity's mass. Use this to create floating platforms, heavy bosses, or light enemies."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((balloon (world/spawn 'balloon 100 100)))\n  (entity/gravity-scale! balloon 0)\n  (world/step))" :note "Balloon floats in place; gravity does not affect it.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(let ((player (world/spawn 'player 100 100))\n      (heavy-block (world/spawn 'block 200 100)))\n  (entity/gravity-scale! player 1)\n  (entity/gravity-scale! heavy-block 3)\n  (entity/set-vel! player 0 -5)\n  (entity/set-vel! heavy-block 0 -5)\n  (world/step)\n  (world/step))" :note "Both entities are launched upward; heavy-block falls back down much faster due to 3x gravity.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (spawn-enemy difficulty)\n  (let ((enemy (world/spawn 'enemy 150 150)))\n    (entity/mass! enemy (+ 1 difficulty))\n    (entity/gravity-scale! enemy (+ 0.5 (* 0.5 difficulty)))\n    (entity/drag! enemy 0.05)\n    enemy))\n(let ((easy-enemy (spawn-enemy 0))\n      (hard-enemy (spawn-enemy 3)))\n  (world/step))" :note "Difficulty scales mass and gravity together, creating a weight-based progression without changing world gravity.")
  )
  :caveats ("Negative gravity scales are allowed but will reverse gravity direction (entity falls upward); use carefully." "Gravity scale is applied every frame; it is not a one-time acceleration." "If world gravity is 0 (no gravity), changing gravity-scale has no effect." "gravity-scale is independent of mass; changing one does not affect the other.")
  :drawbacks ("Gravity scale is a multiplier, not an absolute value; if the world gravity changes, all scales shift proportionally." "No 'natural' falloff over time; gravity scale is constant once set." "Floating entities (scale 0) still obey drag and friction, so they will not truly hover forever if forces push them.")
  :usecases ("Platforms or clouds that float despite world gravity." "Enemy difficulty tuning: heavier enemies feel more imposing and fall faster." "Zero-G or low-G areas: temporarily reduce gravity scale in a region." "Gameplay variety: light enemies (scale 0.5) vs. armored enemies (scale 2).")
  :related ("entity/mass!" "entity/drag!" "world/gravity!" "entity/accel!")
  :learn (:concept "Per-entity gravity tuning independent of world gravity and mass." :prerequisites ("world/spawn" "world/gravity!" "entity/mass!") :progression "Set constant gravity scales first, then combine with entity/mass! and entity/drag! for full embodiment tuning.")
  :row-2-audit (
    :runs "spec-only"
   
    (:problem "A balloon and a rock share the same world but must fall differently. Changing world/gravity! affects everyone; using entity/mass! affects constraints not gravity. Per-body scaling of gravity is the direct answer."
     :program "(define bal (world/spawn 'bal 0 0))\n(define rock (world/spawn 'rock 50 0))\n(entity/gravity-scale! bal 0)\n(entity/gravity-scale! rock 2)\n(world/gravity! 0 0.5)\n(world/step)"
     :explanation "Balloon (scale 0) floats; rock (scale 2) falls twice as fast as default. World gravity is unchanged. The per-body multiplier isolates the tuning to the entity level.")
    (:eng "SRE: per-entity behaviour without global side effects." :math "Multiplicative modulation of gravity vector." :cs "Per-instance override; same shape as CSS's inline style override.")
    :meta "world/gravity! is global; entity/mass! shapes constraint response not gravity. gravity-scale! is the correct verb.")
  :row-3-dimension (
    (:setup "Per-instance coefficient scaling a global effect."
     :rungs (
       (:domain "entity" :code "(entity/gravity-scale! e 2)")
       (:domain "audio"  :code "(define (mix-track vol master) (* vol master))\n(mix-track 0.5 0.8)")
       (:domain "econ"   :code "(define (tax-rate base local) (* base local))\n(tax-rate 0.05 1.2)"))

    (:claim "Zero-scale means gravity does not affect the entity: with gravity-scale 0 and world gravity nonzero, entity vertical velocity unchanged by step."
     :program "(define e (world/spawn 'x 0 0))\n(entity/gravity-scale! e 0)\n(entity/drag! e 0) (entity/set-vel! e 0 0)\n(world/gravity! 0 5) (world/floor!)\n(world/step)\n(display (cadr (entity/vel e)))"
     :invariant "∀ e. gravity-scale(e,0) ⇒ Δvy from gravity = 0"
     :meta "Zero-multiplier annihilates. Falsified if vy changed. book-of-math ch 07 (algebra) grounds.")

(verb
  :name "entity/hp!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/hp! id hp) → void"
  :summary "Set the hit points of an entity; used with entity/damage! for health mechanics."
  :explanation "entity/hp! stores a health value on the entity, typically an integer. This is a game-state property (like any other per-entity value) but is treated specially by entity/damage!: when damage is dealt, HP is subtracted, and if HP drops to 0 or below, the entity emits 'entity/died and is despawned. Use entity/hp! to initialize or reset health, and entity/damage! to subtract health during gameplay."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((monster (world/spawn 'monster 100 100)))\n  (entity/hp! monster 10))" :note "Give the monster 10 hit points.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(let ((boss (world/spawn 'boss 200 200)))\n  (entity/hp! boss 50)\n  (entity/damage! boss 10)\n  (entity/damage! boss 10))" :note "Boss starts with 50 HP; two damage calls subtract 10 each (boss is now at 30 HP and still alive).")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (spawn-scaled-enemy level)\n  (let ((enemy (world/spawn 'enemy 150 150)))\n    (entity/mass! enemy (+ 1 level))\n    (entity/hp! enemy (* 5 (+ 1 level)))\n    (entity/gravity-scale! enemy (+ 1 (* 0.5 level)))\n    enemy))\n(let ((e1 (spawn-scaled-enemy 0))\n      (e2 (spawn-scaled-enemy 2)))\n  (entity/damage! e1 3)\n  (entity/damage! e2 3))" :note "Spawn enemies with scaled HP based on level: level 0 has 5 HP, level 2 has 15 HP. Both take 3 damage but only level 0 is at risk of death.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(entity/hp! 'hero 100)" :note "Set the hero's health to 100. Overwrites whatever it was before.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (revive id)\n  (entity/hp! id 100))\n(on-key\n  (lambda (k)\n    (when (eq? k 'r) (revive 'hero))))" :note "Press R to revive the hero with a full bar.")
  )
  :caveats ("entity/hp! sets the value directly; it does not add or subtract. To modify HP, read with entity/ref first or use entity/damage!." "HP is an arbitrary number; there is no enforcement of positive values (you can set negative HP)." "entity/damage! is the only built-in function that checks HP for death; setting HP directly does not trigger 'entity/died unless you call entity/damage!." "HP is independent of other properties; an entity can have 0 HP and still move or interact.")

  :usecases ("Boss or enemy health bars; each hit reduces HP until death." "Player lives or shield systems; regeneration or temporary invulnerability." "Scaling difficulty: higher-level enemies have higher HP pools." "Tutorial or miniboss patterns: tune HP to match expected player DPS.")
  :related ("entity/damage!" "entity/despawn!" "entity/ref" "entity/set!")

Later, add entity/set! to track healing potions or shields.")
  :row-2-audit (
    (:problem "A monster needs a starting hp of 50 and later damage transitions must trigger death cleanly. Using entity/set! writes to scratch but bypasses death handling; using entity/hp! writes to the special hp slot recognized by entity/damage!."
     :program "(define m (world/spawn 'monster 100 100))\n(entity/hp! m 50)\n(entity/damage! m 60)\n(display (entity/alive? m))"
     :explanation "hp! sets the special slot that damage! reads and checks against zero. Because 60 > 50, damage triggers death and the monster despawns."

  :row-4-proof (

(verb
  :name "entity/kind"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "rd"
  :signature "(entity/kind id) -> symbol"
  :summary "Returns the kind symbol of an entity, or 'entity-not-found if the id is unknown."
  :explanation "Every entity in the world has a kind—a symbol that identifies its type (e.g., 'player, 'coin, 'wall). This is a read-only query; it tells you what class of thing an entity is. If the entity has been despawned or the id was never valid, you get the symbol 'entity-not-found instead of an error, allowing you to branch on it safely."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((player-id 1))\n  (define (check-kind id)\n    (entity/kind id))\n  (check-kind player-id))" :note "Simple lookup of a known entity's kind; returns the symbol stored in the entity record.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define my-world 'my-world)\n(define (spawn-and-describe world kind-name)\n  (let ((new-id (world/spawn world 10 20)))\n    (list 'spawned new-id 'with-kind (entity/kind new-id))))\n(spawn-and-describe my-world 'gem)" :note "After spawning, immediately read the kind back; useful to confirm the entity was created with the right type.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define my-world 'my-world)\n(define (apply-gravity-to-all world)\n  (world/each world\n    (lambda (id)\n      (if (equal? (entity/kind id) 'dynamic)\n        (entity/accel! id 0 -9.8)\n        #f))))\n(apply-gravity-to-all my-world)" :note "Use kind as a dispatch key: loop over all entities and apply a rule only to those matching a certain kind.")
  )
  :caveats ("Returns 'entity-not-found silently; does not throw. Check for this symbol if the id may be stale." "Kind is set at spawn time and cannot be changed; it is immutable." "Unknown ids do not cause an error, so a typo in the id will return 'entity-not-found rather than alerting you.")

  :related ("entity/state" "world/spawn" "world/each" "entity/tag!")

(verb
  :name "entity/layer!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/layer! id bits|name|list) -> void"
  :summary "Set the collision layer bits that define 'what I am' for this entity."
  :explanation "In Motoi's physics, collision is a bitwise dance: each entity has a layer (what it is) and a mask (what it scans for). Layer! sets the layer bits. You can pass a number (bitfield), a symbol (a registered layer name), or a list of symbols. Entities only collide if both sides allow it: A's layer must be in B's mask, AND B's layer must be in A's mask. Layer! is the 'I am' half of that contract."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((hero-id 1))\n  (entity/layer! hero-id 'player)\n  (entity/mask! hero-id '(wall spike)))" :note "Simple setup: mark the hero as a 'player layer, and tell it to scan for 'wall and 'spike.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (make-ghost id)\n  (entity/layer! id 'ghost)\n  (entity/mask! id 'coin))\n(define (make-solid id)\n  (entity/layer! id 'solid)\n  (entity/mask! id '(solid player)))\n(make-ghost 5)\n(make-solid 3)" :note "Two entities with different layer/mask pairs: ghosts only collect coins, solids collide with each other.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (toggle-passthrough id)\n  (let ((current-layer (if (equal? (entity/kind id) 'player)\n                          'player\n                          'intangible)))\n    (entity/layer! id current-layer)\n    (if (equal? current-layer 'intangible)\n      (entity/mask! id '())\n      (entity/mask! id '(solid wall)))))\n(toggle-passthrough 1)" :note "Dynamic layer changes based on kind and state; useful for power-ups or phase shifts.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(entity/layer! 'hero 'player)" :note "Tell the physics engine that this entity belongs to the 'player layer.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(entity/layer! 'arrow '(projectile hostile))" :note "An arrow can belong to multiple layers at once — projectile AND hostile.")
  )
  :caveats ("Layer is 'what I am'; mask is 'what I scan for'. Both must agree for a collision to fire." "Symbol names must match registered layers from collision/define-layers!. (verb
  :name "entity/mask!"
  :library "entity"
  :kind "mut"
  :signature "(entity/mask! id bits|name|list) -> void"
  :summary "Set the collision mask bits that define 'what I scan for' on this entity."
  :explanation "Mask is the second half of Motoi's bitwise collision filter: while layer says 'what I am', mask says 'what kinds of things I can collide with'. You can pass a number (bitfield), a symbol (a registered layer name), or a list of symbols. For a collision to occur, both entity A's layer must match B's mask, and B's layer must match A's mask. Mask! is how you declare interest."
  :examples (
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(let ((coin-id 10))\n  (entity/layer! coin-id 'collectible)\n  (entity/mask! coin-id '()))" :note "Coins don't scan for anything (empty mask), so they never collide; only the player picks them up.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(define (setup-player id)\n  (entity/layer! id 'player)\n  (entity/mask! id '(wall spike coin)))\n(define (setup-enemy id)\n  (entity/layer! id 'enemy)\n  (entity/mask! id '(player wall)))\n(setup-player 1)\n(setup-enemy 2)" :note "Player scans for walls/spikes/coins; enemy scans for player/walls. Collisions fire only when both agree.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "expert" :code "(define (apply-shield id duration)\n  (let ((old-mask (entity/ref id 'shield-mask)))\n    (entity/mask! id '(coin heal))\n    (entity/set! id 'shield-mask old-mask)\n    (after duration\n      (lambda ()\n        (entity/mask! id (or old-mask '(wall spike coin)))))))\n(apply-shield 1 60)" :note "Temporarily shrink the mask during a shield phase, then restore it; demonstrates deferred restoration.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "novice" :code "(entity/mask! 'hero 'enemy)" :note "The hero only scans for collisions with entities on the 'enemy layer.")
    (:dialect "motoi" :tier "intermediate" :code "(entity/mask! 'radar '(hostile boss))" :note "A radar entity looks for both hostile things and bosses, ignoring everything else.")
  )
  :caveats ("Mask alone is not enough; the target's layer must also be in your mask. Both sides must consent." "Symbol names must match registered layers. Unknown symbols become 0 bits (no collision)." "Changes take effect after the next world/step. Mid-step changes do not re-test current contacts." "Passing an empty list or 0 makes the entity never collide (useful for ghosts or triggers that only report).")
  :drawbacks ("Asymmetric filtering can be confusing: A sees B but B doesn't see A means no collision." "No built-in validation; typos in layer names silently fail." "Frequent mask changes are expensive; batch them at phase boundaries rather than per-frame.")
  :usecases ("Spawn-time: declare what each entity type listens for." "Temporary immunity: zero the mask during invincibility frames." "Selective collision: enemies might ignore each other but not the player." "Debugging: toggle mask on/off to see collision behavior.")

  :learn (:concept "The 'receiver' half of collision: what this entity is interested in." :prerequisites ("collision/define-layers!" "entity/layer!") :progression "After entity/layer!, use entity/mask! to complete the pair, then query with entity/collisions.")

     :program "(define p (world/spawn 'player 0 0))\n(entity/layer! p 'player)\n(entity/mask! p '(enemy wall coin))\n(entity/set! p 'saved-mask '(enemy wall coin))\n(entity/mask! p '(wall coin))\n(world/after 180 'shield-off 'player)"
     :explanation "The setup mask lists everything; the shield step narrows it to (wall coin), stashing the previous mask so a later handler on 'shield-off can restore it. The scan filter changes while the layer stays constant."
     :meta "entity/layer! would change what the player IS — everyone else would suddenly see them differently. entity/mask! only changes what the player scans for; a clean local decision that doesn't leak to peers.")
    (:eng "SRE: the saved-mask key is a mini-transaction log — audit lane can replay it to see when immunity turned on/off." :math "Element of a subset lattice under narrow/widen." :cs "Filter narrowing; the receive-half of a pub/sub filter pair."))
  :row-3-dimension (

    (:meta "Shape: interest-filter; subset of the universe the receiver will listen to.")
    (:eng "SRE: narrow filters starve legitimate traffic — always log the mask on suspicious no-events." :math "Subset of a finite universe." :cs "Subscription set; receive-side of pub/sub."))
